title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy

access.edition_or_version: First book edition: Pan Books, London, 1979 (ISBN 0330258648); preceded by the 1978 six-episode BBC radio series

mechanics.premise: The Earth is demolished by a bureaucrats' demolition order, and the last human survivor wanders the galaxy with a demonstrably unreliable reference book as his only authority.
mechanics.deflation_targets: Cosmic and institutional pomposity in rotation — planetary engineering, official procedure, self-important expertise — deflated by being narrated in the same flat register as minor inconveniences.
mechanics.licensed_frame: Established comic science-fiction conventions plus the in-world device of the Guide itself: an encyclopedic voice that licenses deadpan delivery of absurdity as information rather than comment.
mechanics.point_of_view: Close third person around the bewildered everyman, with interpolated pseudo-reference entries from the Guide.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Expectation-collapse as house style: grand setups answered by bureaucratic or domestic banality; understatement carrying the deflation instead of punchlines; satirically characterized premise confirmed via the SFE entry.
mechanics.dialogue: Characters play sincere straight men to an insane status quo — officials explain absurd procedures politely, which does the mocking without the narrator sneering.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Wonder repeatedly built up and deflated into inconvenience; grief at the opening loss is itself processed through the flat register, which is the boundary edge of the tone.
mechanics.boundaries_and_restraint: Adjacent to satirical-literature: the SFE entry describes the work's premise as satirically characterized, so the card should treat it as irreverent voice operating over satirical content rather than a pure exemplar.
mechanics.conventions: Canonicalizes the comic-science-fiction narration mode: cosmic stakes rendered in underwhelmed prose.
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Makes the reference-book deadpan a load-bearing comic voice — reverence for information punctured by the information itself.
mechanics.critical_reception: Grew from 1978 radio to 1979 novel and enduring canonical status in comic SF; the SFE entry treats Adams as a major figure of British SF humor.
mechanics.audience_reception: Continuous multi-format afterlife (radio, novel, TV, stage) — its deflations remain cultural reference points.
